paper.title: Algorithm 462: Bivariate normal distribution (BIVNOR)
paper.venue: Communications of the ACM 16(10), Oct 1973, p. 638; collected as TOMS Algorithm 462
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/462.gz (ACM article not read; ACM pages return 403 from this sandbox)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 462.gz, shar created 2005-12-15 (fetched by scout 2026-11-27 into /tmp/scout-462, unpacked as text, not executed)
code.note: Shell archive. Members of interest: Fortran/Dp/Drivers/driver.f (program TOMS462_PRB calling BIVNOR), Fortran/Dp/Drivers/Makefile (target Res runs the driver into Res), Fortran/Dp/Drivers/res (the shipped output), Fortran/Dp/Src/src.f (BIVNOR) and Fortran/Dp/Src/erf.f. The rerun must unpack the shar and compile src.f, erf.f and driver.f.

claim.location: Shipped output res (Fortran/Dp/Drivers/res inside 462.gz): the first data row of the BIVNOR table, H=0.80000, K=-1.50000, R=-0.90000, BIVNOR column 0.147355 (EXPECT column 0.148000). The driver computes cdf = bivnor(ah, ak, r) and prints it with g14.6.

reference.sha256: not recorded: the shipped text is line-split from the shar; rerun should compare the member

claim.metric: BIVNOR(h=0.8, k=-1.5, r=-0.9), the standard bivariate normal cumulative distribution function as returned by src.f
claim.paper_value: Shipped reference output res, row 1: 0.147355. The paper's table is not read here; the EXPECT column in the driver (0.148) is a 3-digit value and is not the claim.

tolerance.basis: The printed value has six decimal places (g14.6 gives six significant digits here), so its rounding half-unit is 5e-7. Set before any run and not to be loosened after a run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: one BIVNOR call per row, six rows in the driver.
cost.data_licence: No data. Public netlib TOMS archive.

why: BIVNOR is a numerical quadrature/series evaluation of a non-closed-form integral, so the single printed value at (0.8, -1.5, -0.9) tests a port of the method, not a paper-derivable number.
